rv.q: Much crucial work has been done since the Chicago tryout, successful as it was.

What Harvey Fierstein and Cyndi Lauper have fashioned is a sweet, if formulaic, evening that manages to be both brazen and innocent.

With Mr. Porter, as Lola, and Stark Sands, as Charlie, back on stage together for a limited run through January, “Kinky Boots” feels like Broadway’s hottest new musical, rather than one five years into its run.
Kinky Boots and its cast get a standing ovation because they have earned and deserve it.
Kinky Boots, a winning musical to celebrate and applaud.
Despite the fact that this show feels familiar, it is successfully hilarious and engaging.
Still, there is nothing wrong with feeling good, and this show does that shamelessly.
Kinky Boots is a feel-good musical that succeeds in being both entertaining and emotionally resonant.
Kinky Boots may not be as dazzling as the footwear on the show’s drag queens, but it’s certainly well-constructed, holds up under pressure, and will give you an entertaining two-and-a-half-hour walk.
